record.original_question: Modify the continuous guessing game by allowing the hider to move from one secret number h_n to the next h_{n+1} between consecutive guesses, and score the hider by Σ|g_n-h_∞|, where h_∞ is the limiting value of the hider's secret numbers. The source states that Alpern's pure minimax strategy still works for this payoff. Can one prove that this pure minimax strategy is actually optimal for the moving-hider version of the game?

evidence.quote: One can modify the continuous guessing game following Gilbert, by allowing the hider to move from one secret number hn to the next hn+1 between consecu- tive guesses. There are various choices for the payoff: it could be either ∑ |gn −hn| or ∑ |gn −h∞|,w h e r eh∞ denotes the limiting value of the hider’s secret numbers.

Alpern’s pure minimax strategy still works for the payoff ∑ |gn −h∞ |, even though the hider has a larger strategy space. It should be easier to prove that the pure min- imax strategy is optimal in this case.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following two-player zero-sum continuous guessing game between a Hider and a Guesser. At each step n = 1, 2, 3, ..., the Hider selects a real number h_n ∈ ℝ (which may differ from h_{n-1}), and the Guesser, without observing h_n, announces a guess g_n ∈ ℝ. After each guess, the Hider truthfully reveals whether g_n < h_n, g_n = h_n, or g_n > h_n. The sequence (h_n) is assumed to converge to a limit h_∞ ∈ ℝ. The Hider's strategy space therefore allows the secret to move between consecutive guesses, subject only to the comparison responses already given and to the existence of the limit h_∞. The payoff (paid by the Guesser to the Hider) is
    P = Σ_{n=1}^{∞} |g_n - h_∞|.
The Guesser seeks to minimize P and the Hider seeks to maximize it.

In the classical static version of this game (where h_n = h is fixed), Alpern's pure minimax strategy for the Guesser is known to be optimal. The same pure minimax strategy is still well-defined when the Hider is allowed to move, and it yields a finite value against any admissible Hider strategy with payoff Σ |g_n - h_∞|.

Prove that Alpern's pure minimax Guesser strategy is optimal (i.e. achieves the value of the game) in this moving-hider variant with payoff Σ |g_n - h_∞|.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface any published proof that Alpern's pure minimax strategy is optimal in the moving-hider variant of the continuous guessing game with payoff Σ|g_n - h_∞|. The question is listed among open problems in search games, and no later resolution was found in available sources.
